embeds.title: 🔴 Underminr Vulnerability Lets Attackers Hide Malicious Connections Behind Trusted Domains
embeds.description:
ADAMnetworks reports that threat actors are exploiting a vulnerability called Underminr in shared CDN infrastructure to hide connections to malicious domains. The vulnerability, a variant of domain fronting, allows attackers to present an SNI and HTTP Host of a trusted domain while forcing requests to a different IP address on the same shared edge. ADAMnetworks reports the technique has been abused in attacks targeting large-scale hosting providers and can be used to hide C&C server connections, VPN/proxy connections, and circumvent network egress policies. Approximately 88 million domains are potentially affected, with internet infrastructure in the US, UK, and Canada most impacted.
**Sources:** SecurityWeek • 🔴 1 corroborating
**CVEs:** none • **Access:** n/a
**Incident date:** unknown • **Confidence:** claim
